text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Newfoundland Premier Brian Tobin issues Churchill warning: Newfoundland will pull plug on hydroelectric contract if Quebec secedes, Tobin says.
- Ontario surgeons to charge patients new fees: Orthopedists shift paperwork costs.
- Commmitment fades for aid mission: Western nations meeting over next few days to re-evaluate scope of operation.
- U.S. stands alone in UN balloting: Only No vote against Boutros-Ghali.
- Youngsters paid $1 for making $50 balls: Despite official denials, child labour remains important part of Pakistan's export business.
- Altamira takeover challenged: Shareholders go to court to block Manulife's $660-million bid, say better deal coming.
- Trimark kings plan massive stock sale.
- Bank of Montreal to open Beijing branch: First Canadian bank approved.
- Unemployment Insurance premium reduction assailed: Business, labour united in attacking Ottawa's modest cut.
- Altamira takeover sideswiped: Founding investors seek injunction to block Manulife Financial's bid for the mutual fund giant, saying a better offer is on the way.
- Ottawa cuts payroll taxes, but business wants more.
